title: AWS Transcribe Pricing: Batch, Streaming Rates (2026)
summary: AWS Transcribe pricing charges per minute of audio processed.
body_markdown:
## Automating the work around Transcribe with Activepieces


Transcribe itself gets no cheaper with Activepieces: AWS sets that price, and the tool only moves files and results around it.


What it can do is automate the steps before and after a Transcribe job, and because every plan includes unlimited flows, the number of such pipelines you build adds nothing to the bill.


### What the workflow does


Think of Activepieces as a workflow builder.


You chain a trigger and a series of steps on a canvas, and each step can call an app from the 747 integrations in its open source monorepo, apply a condition, loop over items, or hand a task to an AI agent.


Nothing about the homepage example below has to do with audio; it is a sales-lead flow.


It shows the shape of the thing: a trigger at the top, an AI qualification step, a yes/no condition, then actions such as adding a record, posting a notification and sending an email, joined by vertical lines that show the order.


Swap the lead for an audio file and the same pattern fits a transcription pipeline. A new file landing in an S3 bucket or a Drive folder triggers the flow. The next step starts a Transcribe job.


Once the transcript is finished, a later step picks it up and sends it onward, to a document, a message or a database.


You should check whether a ready-made step exists for your exact Transcribe call before assuming it does. Where one doesn't, a generic request step can usually cover it, at the cost of more setup.


### What it does not change


However you automate it, every minute Transcribe bills is still billed by AWS at AWS's rates. The tiers, the rounding of short clips, the add-on charges and the quotas all apply exactly as before.


Activepieces, whose Free plan costs $0, gives no discount on them, and it doesn't tell you what your audio will cost.


It also adds a second bill. Activepieces has its own pricing, separate from AWS, so automating the plumbing means pricing two things instead of one.


That second bill is easy to price, though: the Activepieces pricing page lists 1 credit per flow run, whatever the number of steps, set against the per-task billing on Zapier's pricing page and the per-module billing on Make's.


A pipeline of S3 trigger, Transcribe job, Slack message and CRM update therefore costs the same credit as a two-step version of it.


If a workflow saves an hour of manual handling a week, that saving is real. It belongs in your cost model next to both invoices, not in place of the per-workload estimate the earlier sections argued for.
